newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says 3.0 pct EMU deficit target to remain.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says 3.0 pct EMU deficit target to remain.

text.p: Finance Minster Theo Waigel, responding to press reports he had weakened his stance on the deficit criterion for European Monetary Union (EMU), said he opposes any looser interpretation of the rule.

Prospective EMU participants' goal of reducing their public sector deficits to three percent of gross domestic product should not be watered down, he told reporters before a top-level meeting of his Christian Social Union.
"3.0 percent is 3.0 percent, and it will stay that way," he said.
Waigel said the press reports that he had eased his strict stance were "unfair in the highest degree", adding that he sees no leeway for interpretation on the deficit rule.
Earlier, a ministry spokeswoman said Waigel had maintained his advocacy of a strict interpretation of the Maastricht rules throughout the weekend meeting of EU Finance Ministers in the Netherlands.

Two British dailies, the Guardian and the Financial Times, reported from the meeting that Waigel had shifted his stance, quoting him as saying: "I have never nailed myself to the cross of three percent".
The Guardian quoted Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn saying the words were "probably the most important which have been said during the weekend".
